text: Mass implied by the observed pull (log, M☉)
finding: Plain-layer axis label (and the plain Mass-view note 'how much mass the observed pull implies within each distance') states that the observed pull implies a mass. That reads the discrepancy as mass, the reading the Methods page rejects for 'mass discrepancy'. The plain note also drops the expert caveat that this is 'a convention, not the true enclosed mass'. Suggest 'Observed pull written as a mass, M = g r²/G (a convention)'.

text: log M_obs(<r) = g_obs r² / G (M☉)
finding: Calling g_obs r²/G an 'observed mass' (M_obs; legend line 'M_obs = M_bar'; tooltip 'M_obs(<r)') presents a convention as a measured mass and favours mass-based readings. Suggest a neutral symbol such as M_g,obs or 'g_obs r²/G', with the convention named in the axis label.

text: Enclosed-mass profiles and dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratios are standard in mass modelling.
finding: The Mass lens is described in 'dynamical mass' terms with no plain counterpart that keeps the convention caveat. Inside the Atlas's own description this is the mass framing it rejects elsewhere. Suggest stating it as a convention used by mass-modelling studies, in both layers.

text: Detected share
finding: Plain label for g_bar/g_obs (lower budget panel; reference line 'all of the observed pull'). A 'share' implies the observed pull is a sum of parts, with the undetected remainder as another part. That assumes an additive extra component, which is a cause. Suggest 'Detected ÷ observed' or 'Ratio, detected to observed'.

text: Detected share
finding: Same label as on aeg-s-000124, with the same issue: g_bar/g_obs is presented as a share of the observed pull.

text: Shown as a limit on anomalous acceleration, not a point (D-028)
finding: 'Anomalous' is an evaluative word that presumes a deviation from expected physics. Suggest 'a limit on any acceleration beyond the Newtonian (ephemeris) prediction'.

text: Pull budget
finding: A 'budget' frames g_obs as a total to be filled by components, so the gap reads as a missing item. That framing suits additive-component accounts more than accounts that change the force law. Plain uses the neutral 'Observed pull and the pull from detected matter'; the expert heading, the section links and the aria label ('detected baryonic components stacked … their sum g_bar') could use the same. Also on aeg-s-000071.

text: Distances. Flat ΛCDM in each source's own cosmology, with radiation neglected
finding: Names a cosmological model that contains one account (cold dark matter) outside a quotation, the confrontations section or a source's fitting-function name. Suggest 'a flat cosmology with each source's H0 and Ω_m (Ω_Λ = 1 − Ω_m)'. The same unquoted wording is on methods/aeg-d-strong-lensing ('in a flat ΛCDM cosmology with the H₀ and Ω_m the source states'), on the lens dataset page and on systems aeg-s-000412 and aeg-s-000614 ('Distances in the flat ΛCDM cosmology stated by the source of each θ_E'). On the KiDS page it is a quotation and is fine.

text: plus an assumed hot-gas halo for the variant
finding: 'Halo' is used as description (here and in 'Hot gas: absent, or modelled (the authors' assumed halo, hot-gas variant only; D-034)' and 'for the hot-gas rows, the assumed halo'). The changelog (T4) said this package text would change at re-issue, and v3 is that re-issue. Suggest 'assumed hot-gas component'.

text: D-097 classes, the 64 systems with rows: 8 findings (recorded, not plotted), 14 possibilities (plotted, with the quotation), 42 with no relevant statement.
finding: Systems are taken off the map because their sources state they are out of equilibrium or tidally disrupted. Such statements are often interpretations made inside one account (for example, tides invoked to explain a high or a low dispersion), so this removal can shape the picture in a way that is not account-neutral. Suggest a map toggle that shows the 8 with a distinct mark, so readers can see what the rule removes.

text: Atlas of Extra Gravitation
finding: The site name says there is 'extra' gravitation. That is a result, and not a uniform one: the same site shows g_obs/g_bar below 1 for globular clusters (for example NGC 362, 0.41). This is a ruled name, so it is flagged for the record. At the least, the About page could say once that the name does not assert an excess everywhere.

text: Extra pull: observed pull ÷ pull from detected matter. 1 means they are equal; below 1, the observed pull is less.
finding: The plain name for the ratio carries the result: a quantity named 'extra pull' can equal 1 (none extra) or fall below 1 (less pull). The same label is the plain y-axis of the map's Ratio and Scale views ('Extra pull (log of observed ÷ detected)'). Suggest 'pull ratio' (observed ÷ detected).

text: v1.0 plots a system with its own redshift only if that redshift, as printed by the source, is below 0.30 (D-066).
finding: Redshift, a continuous property, is thresholded for plotting. The stated reason ('baryon inventories at high redshift often rely on scaling relations') is general and unsourced, and does not obviously hold for strong lenses, whose stellar masses come from the same SPS fits at any z. Suggest giving a source for the reason, or plotting z ≥ 0.30 lenses behind an off-by-default toggle with redshift as a colour.

text: No comparison of this kind is free of theory. The Atlas compares observed quantities with a declared reference calculation: Newtonian gravity on the baryons each source detected, and General Relativity for turning a lensing signal into an acceleration.
finding: The expert stance names GR as part of the reference for lensing, and also the symmetry rule and the five site layers. The plain version ('Any comparison needs a yardstick … Newton's gravity from the matter that was detected') says the yardstick is Newton only and leaves the rest out. The two layers state different baselines.

text: From smallest to largest: the Solar System, pairs of stars far apart, young star clusters, old star clusters, spinning disc galaxies, small faint round galaxies, round and lens-shaped galaxies, galaxies in unusual shapes or settings, groups of galaxies, clusters of galaxies, and colliding clusters.
finding: The plain layer drops the kinds table ('Switch to the technical view for the full table'), and sections 5a–5c and 'What the survey shows' appear in the plain layer only as the expert text.

text: Distances here are for the systems on the map.
finding: Plain caption for the continuous-axes table, but the expert caption says 'systems below the epoch cut only', and the table counts recorded rows that are not on the map (Baumgardt GCs '155 clusters', '79'; Strong lenses '147'; KiDS '45'). The plain caption is wrong, and neither layer says the counts include unplotted rows.

text: The description is on GitHub (linked below).
finding: The technical layer gives no description for any issue. For #222, #225, #227, #232 and #234 the plain layer says 'The technical view gives the details and the evidence', so each layer points to the other and neither describes the issue on the page.

text: How tilted the disc is as we see it. It changes the observed pull of the whole galaxy at once. It can be changed with a slider on the map.
finding: The plain layer says distance and tilt are set 'on the map', but the expert layer ('Sliders on this page: … Distance; Inclination') and the map ('Distance and tilt are set one galaxy at a time, on its own page') say they are set on the galaxy's page. Same text on aeg-s-000071.

text: Every kind of matter the dataset considers
finding: The plain heading sits over the expert baryon-inventory text, copied verbatim ('Spitzer [3.6] surface photometry; V_disk and V_bul released for Υ = 1 …'). The plain measurements table also keeps the expert headers (g_obs, −/+ σ). Same on aeg-s-000071.

text: Notes on this galaxy’s numbers
finding: The plain layer repeats the expert flag text verbatim ('beyond_source_range: Metallicity at or below the lowest tabulated …', 'rh_semimajor_assumed …'), and the status values stay in expert notation (g_obs at r½, Υ_V). The same pattern is on aeg-s-000380.

text: An old, dense ball of stars in our galaxy. Kept in the record but not shown on the map, for the reasons below.
finding: The plain layer states that Crater is a globular cluster, while the expert reasons say its 'classification disputed by sources: A7, ambiguous (D-038 4A)'. The plain reasons list is also expert jargon.

text: stellar mass not in the source; g_bar bounded below by gas only; recorded under D-090
finding: The plain layer shows the expert exclusion reason and the known-issue title ('#129: X-COP v2 stage 2 blocked …') unchanged. Same on aeg-s-000187.

text: It had been switched on by our web host without our noticing; this is now fixed and disclosed.
finding: The expert layer says the counter is now active for all countries and the paragraph has been corrected. The plain 'now fixed' can be read as 'switched off'. The two layers can be read as saying different things about whether visits are counted.

text: If we have missed earlier work like this, please tell us.
finding: The plain layer leaves out the expert claim ('In a search on 2026-11-06 (UTC) we found no earlier work that puts globular clusters, dwarf galaxies, disc galaxies, galaxy lensing and galaxy clusters on one g_obs–g_bar plot') and adds 'nothing assumed about the cause', which the expert version does not say.

text: Points that match
finding: The expert label is 'Points with no flag' (99 %, 3,711 of 3,750). Flags include source quality caveats, not only reproduction mismatches, so 'match' overstates. The count 3,750 also differs from the 3,734 on the home page and the 3,837 on Methods, with no explanation.

text: How strongly things pull, compared with what their visible matter should give
finding: The plain home page uses 'visible matter' and 'stars and gas we can see', but the plain vocabulary on Methods is 'pull from detected matter'. Much of the counted gas (atomic HI, X-ray gas) is not visible, and 'visible' invites the contrast 'invisible matter'.

text: The full step-by-step method, with every constant and where each number is read, is in the expert view of this page.
finding: The plain layer of each per-dataset methods page is a three-line summary that sends readers to the expert view, so plain and expert do not say the same thing. The same pattern is on all six methods/aeg-d-* pages.

text: Disc galaxies dominate the current measurements (3,391 of 3,837).
finding: 3,837 counts recorded rows; the home page and the map say 3,734 measurements plotted. The page does not say which count this is or where it comes from.

text: 45 stacked bins of isolated galaxies (Brouwer et al. 2021).
finding: The page does not say that only 22 of the 45 bins are plotted (home: '22 stacked bins'). The reason (isolation limit; hot-gas variant) is given only on the dataset page.

text: X-COP. g_obs: the source’s one-sigma mass errors.
finding: This contradicts the X-COP dataset and methods pages ('The confidence level of the errors is not stated by the source'; 'level not given by the source'). The general line 'Error bars are one sigma.' is likewise wrong for X-COP and for the lens rows with no stated level.

text: g_obs from the non-parametric hydrostatic reconstruction
finding: D-119 corrected this: 'the source does not state that the released g_obs is its nonparametric reconstruction', and methods/aeg-d-xcop says 'Which method the released GOBS comes from is not stated'. The claim still stands here and on the X-COP dataset page ('GOBS as released (the source's non-parametric hydrostatic g_obs)').

text: McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert 2016, arXiv:1610.08981, eq. 2
finding: Wrong attribution. Every other page gives arXiv:1610.08981 as Lelli, McGaugh, Schombert & Pawlowski 2017, ApJ 836, 152. McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert 2016 is the PRL paper, which About lists separately.

text: van Hemert, J. (2026). Atlas of Extra Gravitation, version 0.1 (preliminary, not peer reviewed). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23864356
finding: The citation offered is v0.1, but the page says v0.2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24017479) is the last release. Readers are sent to an outdated version.

text: Reproduction: passed
finding: Each current version shows 'passed', but that is its re-issue test (T1–T7). The comparison with the source that failed carries over unchanged (SPARC: 4 points, #8; X-COP part A). The badge does not lead to the failed source comparison.

text: Putman et al. 2021 Table 1, None
finding: The gas-limit input has no usable route to its row in the source (known issue #232), yet it is shown as a source locator on the page.

text: v0.2 is preliminary and not peer reviewed. An audit of 254 randomly sampled rows, read by AI agents, found no wrong values, but did not pass on source records and methods text.
finding: This summary (in both layers) leaves out that the audit also failed on neutrality (4 must-fix and about 120 should-fix findings, per the About changelog). The audit result is reported only in part.
